name: medrano_enrichment_brief_2026_10_29
prompt:
Goal: make the Medrano Partners lead sheet something John Knox (founder/CEO of Medrano Partners, medranopartners.com, an AI strategy firm for churches and faith orgs, ex Gloo) could not have built himself. Caleb Newton and Gavin Munroe (Firm Foundation) will hand it to him after an NDA is signed.

Inputs:
- ~/Downloads/Medrano leads/Medrano leads.csv: 596 rows, columns tier,fit,why_now_score,hold,kind,org,city,state,website,revenue,size,stack,buyer,buyer_title,buyer_email,buyer_source,why_now,why_now_date,why_now_source,tier_rationale. Work on the 145 rows with tier 1 or 2 only.
- ~/Downloads/Medrano leads/work/: the pipeline that built it (build_list.py uses ~/.chewbacca/kit/current/tools/gtme_score.py; church_whynow.py, whynow.csv, whynow-full.jsonl hold the earlier why-now pass). Read these first and reuse them. Use gtme_score.signal_strength for why-now strength, and HOLD anything under 6. Read ~/code/chewbacca/skills/gtm-engineering/SKILL.md and its references for the rules (there's a lesson there from 10/27 where a hand-rolled scorer matched a baseball trade as a church's why-now: check every signal is actually about that org).
- Today only 16 of 596 rows have a why-now, 160 a buyer, 42 a buyer email.

Do, for each of the 145:
1. Find a dated 2026 why-now about THAT org, with its URL: new senior/exec pastor or ED, a tech/ops/data/IT job posting, a capital or building campaign, merger or new campus, AI/data/cyber news, big growth. Web search, the org's own site/news/careers page, and the Exa tools (mcp__togari__togari_exa_search) are all fine. Nothing guessed. No date or no source means leave it blank.
2. Fill a buyer and buyer email ONLY when published on the org's own site. Never guess an email pattern.
3. Add a column "Medrano fit": which ONE Medrano service fits and a one-line reason tied to the why-now. Read medranopartners.com first for their real service names (AI governance and policy with a faith track, AI training, custom AI builds, comms and writing, project management; verify).
4. Add a column "First email": 3 to 4 plain sentences John could send, naming the specific why-now. No hype words, no em dashes, no "it's not X, it's Y". Leave blank if there's no why-now.

Output:
- Write ~/Downloads/Medrano leads/Medrano leads enriched.csv (all original columns plus medrano_fit, first_email). Don't overwrite Medrano leads.csv.
- Rebuild the Google Sheet in place. The formatter is /private/tmp/claude-501/mk.py (run it from ~/Downloads/Medrano leads; it reads 'Medrano leads.csv'). Copy it, point it at the enriched CSV, drop tier 3 (C) rows entirely from the client copy, and add the Medrano fit and First email columns right after Why now on the Ready to call and All leads tabs. Update the Start here numbers to whatever is true. Then upload over the existing sheet: `gws drive files update --params '{"fileId":"11vwIPQcLa0b6Nv2bImACMWwge8kK3XFYfn7snZ_P2p8"}' --upload "<xlsx>" --upload-content-type application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`. Do NOT turn link sharing back on. It stays private until the NDA is signed.
- Verify by reading the sheet back with `gws sheets spreadsheets values get`.

Rules: don't email or contact anyone. Don't touch other repos or other tabs' files. Use `chewbacca jobs submit --net` only if you need a long crawl, otherwise just do it. If you run out of road on some rows, keep them blank and count them.

Report back: fill rates before and after for why_now, buyer, buyer_email, medrano_fit and first_email across the 145; 3 example rows that are the strongest; and anything you couldn't do and why. Be honest about blanks.
why: the real 10/29 Medrano brief: named gtme_score and Togari Exa but sent buyers, emails and copy to web search

name: programs_gap_research_2026_10_28
prompt:
Gap-finding research task. A file at "/Users/joelnewton/Downloads/Programs like Discipulus.md" lists ~290 programs, funds, grants, perks and communities for a 19-year-old Christian, autistic USC sophomore founder in LA (companies: Firm Foundation, AI for churches; Anchored, a church platform; later an autism nonprofit). Read it fully first.

Your job: find what it's MISSING by mining curated master lists, not by guessing. Sources to mine: GitHub awesome-lists (awesome-fellowships, awesome-startup-credits, student-opportunities, ai-fellowships-and-residencies by landedjobs, startup-perks lists), Notion/Airtable databases of student founder programs, Merge Club microgrant guide (mergeclub.substack.com), justmovetosf.com equity-free money guide, questd.ai residencies list, opc.community funding list, finta.ai accelerator master list, Notre Dame Founders Club resources page, Reddit r/startups r/EntrepreneurRideAlong threads on student founder programs, "every fellowship for young founders 2026" style posts on X/Substack/Medium, techloy fellowships 2026, Dani Goeppert's Christian Founder's Roadmap, Faith Driven Entrepreneur "Top Capacity Builders" page.

For every candidate, check it against the file (search by name) and keep ONLY ones not already there. Verify each new one on its own site (live and current, 2026-27). Return a list (aim 40+) grouped by type: name, URL, what it gives, who for (does a US undergrad sophomore qualify?), deadline/status, source list you found it in, verified yes/partial. No em dashes. Don't apply to or contact anything.

name: anchored_landing_research_2026_10_28
prompt:
Research task, read-only, no sign-ins, no form submits. I'm building the landing page for Anchored, a startup building "the operating system for every Christian, starting with churches": a church gets one text number, anyone it meets texts a word and gets their next step in WhatsApp or SMS, the pastor sees who is connected to a real person, and later each Christian gets one identity for giving, groups, prayer and Scripture across every church and device (an AI layer across their whole digital life).

Go through the FaithTech website (faithtech.com and its subpages: Labs, projects, challenges, hackathons, articles/blog, "redemptive technology" material, the SoCal hackathon page, any idea or problem lists) and also github.com/FaithTechGlobalLabs (especially faithtech-socal-hackathon, its track docs and README). Use WebFetch/WebSearch or the fetch tool. Read the pages fully.

Return, in under 700 words:
1. Every concrete product idea, problem statement or track brief you find that relates to churches, discipleship, giving, community, AI in ministry, or a "Christian OS" (one line each, with the URL).
2. FaithTech's own language and principles about redemptive technology that a page aimed at pastors and investors could honestly echo (quote under 15 words each, with URL; max 4 quotes).
3. Any stat with a named source about churches, discipleship, loneliness, or follow-up that appears there (number, source, URL).
Mark anything you couldn't open. Do not invent anything; if a page fails to load, say so.

name: yc_speedrun_research_2026_10_28
prompt:
Research how to write a winning YC (W27, due Mon Nov 2 2026 8pm PT) and a16z speedrun (SR008, due Sun Nov 1 11:59pm PT) application, plus quick notes for Basis Fellowship, Emergent Ventures and Inflection Grants. The applicants: Caleb Newton and Gavin Munroe, two part-time USC-area college students, applying with Anchored (text-based follow-up for churches, vision: the OS for every Christian, "Shopify for the church"). Prototype on test data only, no users, no revenue. Already known (don't re-report): YC's howtoapply page (be concise, simplest words first sentence, impressive-thing can't be the startup, show insight + obstacles) and speedrun FAQ (team section weighs most, prefers co-founders, students/part-time ok).

Find what practitioners say beyond those pages: YC partners (Michael Seibel, Dalton Caldwell, Harj Taggar, Paul Graham, Garry Tan) on how they read apps, the founder video, idea-stage/no-traction apps, students, what gets an interview; published accepted YC applications and teardowns; a16z speedrun partners' posts (Andrew Chen, Jon Lai) on what they look for; any faith-tech or church-software companies that got into YC or speedrun, and how they pitched. Use yt-transcript (on PATH: `yt-transcript "<url>"`) for YouTube, never WebFetch a YouTube URL. Prefer primary sources; quote under 15 words per source, attribute everything with URL.

Write the result to /Users/joelnewton/Downloads/YC and speedrun research 10-28.md: (1) 10 to 15 concrete rules with source each, (2) what this specifically means for Anchored's application given no traction and two part-time students, as specific edits, (3) red flags to avoid, (4) a "fastest traction before Sunday" list partners say counts (LOIs, design partners, waitlists). No em dashes anywhere, no emojis, plain sentences. Don't edit any other file and don't submit or contact anything. Report back a 5-line summary.

name: anchored_insight_2026_10_28
prompt:
Goal: find the sharpest, most non-obvious insight for Anchored's YC/a16z speedrun application, one a partner hasn't heard before. Anchored (repo ~/code/personal/anchored, read README.md, SPEC.md, ANCHORED-APP-SPEC.md, docs/) is a church text number: anyone a church meets texts one word and gets next steps one message at a time in WhatsApp/SMS, the church sees who's connected vs quiet; vision is the OS for every Christian (one identity for giving, groups, prayer, Scripture across churches), Shopify-for-the-church route. Built Oct 24 2026 at the FaithTech SoCal x Baptize The World hackathon.

Caleb's brief, his words: "Go through EVERYTHING from the faithtech day and think through all the problems with current church/ministry systems do some research - filling out forms are the WORST and connect cards often fall though and there's no sense of feeling connected other than Sunday and the day of life group go ham bro we gotta have a perspective they hadn't thought of". Also: "AI can power the church to be more faithful".

Step 1, mine what exists (read fully): ~/Downloads/FaithTech call prep.md, ~/Downloads/FF research 10-27.md, ~/Downloads/FF church software and target list.md if present, anything in ~/second-brain and ~/code/chewbacca/team/memory matching faithtech|hackathon|baptize|anchored|connect card (grep -ril), and the anchored repo docs. Note the real quotes from people at the hackathon (e.g. the "Baptism Buddies" mentor, Travis at FaithTech: "completed chapter one doesn't matter").

Step 2, research outside with real sources: connect card follow-up failure rates, first-time guest return rates, how long churches take to follow up, assimilation/retention stats (Barna, Lifeway Research, Faith Communities Today, Hartford Institute, Church Growth/Nelson Searcy "first-time guest" numbers, Planning Center/Pushpay data posts), small-group participation, how much of a congregation is ever in a group, volunteer burnout, form abandonment, how Gen Z experiences church belonging, loneliness data. Prefer primary sources, record URL + exact number + year for every stat. Never WebFetch YouTube; use `yt-transcript "<url>"` if needed.

Step 3, produce 3 candidate insights that are each (a) true per the sources, (b) surprising to a VC, (c) explain why incumbents (Pushpay, Subsplash, Gloo, Planning Center, Text In Church) structurally can't fix it, (d) make Anchored the obvious answer. Example shape only: "churches measure attendance, but the unit that predicts staying is a named relationship, and no church system stores relationships." Rank them and pick one, with a 2-sentence version for the YC "what do you understand that others don't" answer and a 1-sentence version for a video. Also give a sharper, specific version of "AI can power the church to be more faithful" grounded in the sources.

Write to /Users/joelnewton/Downloads/Anchored insight 10-28.md. No em dashes anywhere, no emojis, plain sentences, every number sourced, mark anything unsourced. Don't edit other files, don't submit or contact anything. Return a 6-line summary with the chosen insight verbatim.
